manifest.source: the public read API, bounded exactly as any client reads it

population_census.excluded_because: 575 metres. Every relation a metre has runs to the mantras composed in it, and this view holds no mantras, so all 575 would be drawn unconnected. The metre layer is worth seeing against the corpus rather than against the entity layer.

4,825 recurring wordings. Their interest is how far each one reaches across the four collections, which the formula surface shows directly. As points in a spatial view they would outnumber every other kind of thing by three to one.

720 families of shared wording. Every relation a family has runs to its formulas, which this view excludes, so all 720 would be drawn unconnected. That would read as a finding about the corpus and it is a fact about this projection.

manifest.scope_statement: This view holds the corpus's entity layer and the relations between its members. It is not the whole graph: passages, their containment and their text surfaces are excluded, and so are formulas. An absence here is an absence from the entity layer only.
manifest.truncation_statement: Where a node's fan-out on a predicate reached the API's cap of 50, its edges on that predicate are a sample. Those nodes and predicates are named on the node itself.

nodes.label: Agni
nodes.description: The sacrificial fire, at once the carrier of the offering up to the gods and the divine priest who performs the rite.

nodes.label: Indra
nodes.description: The champion of the gods, who slays Vrtra with the vajra, releases the pent-up waters and rules as king of the pantheon.

nodes.label: Soma
nodes.description: The pressed plant and its exhilarating juice, the offering that is itself a god, addressed as king of plants and lord of the rite.

nodes.label: the Maruts
nodes.description: The storm troop, sons of Rudra, who ride the winds in glittering armour and bring the rain.

nodes.label: the Asvins
nodes.description: The twin horsemen who arrive at daybreak in their chariot and act as the physicians and rescuers of gods and men.

nodes.label: the Waters
nodes.description: The Waters as goddesses, mothers who purify and who are asked for the remedy that they carry.

nodes.label: Varuna
nodes.description: The sovereign who watches over truth and oath, binds the guilty with his fetters and releases the penitent, and whose domain runs to the waters and the encompassing sea.

nodes.label: Brhaspati
nodes.description: The divine priest and lord of prayer, whose formulated word splits open the Vala cave and releases the imprisoned cows.

nodes.label: Usas
nodes.description: The Dawn as a goddess, daughter of heaven, who uncovers the light, rouses the sleeping and is praised in some of the most admired hymns in the corpus.

nodes.label: Pusan
nodes.description: The guardian of roads and herds, who finds what is lost, protects the traveller, and conducts the dead along the path to the Fathers.

nodes.label: Prthivi
nodes.description: The Earth as a goddess, the broad one, most often invoked as the mother beside Dyaus the father.

nodes.label: Savitr
nodes.description: The Impeller, the vivifying power of the sun that sets gods and men in motion at the day's beginning and end, invoked in the most repeated verse of the tradition.

nodes.label: Surya
nodes.description: The sun as a god, the visible disc that crosses the sky drawn by his horses and is called the eye of Mitra and Varuna.

nodes.label: the Adityas
nodes.description: The sons of Aditi, the sovereign gods led by Mitra and Varuna who keep watch over the ordinances.

nodes.label: the Fathers
nodes.description: The ancestral dead, invoked to come to their offering and sit on the strewn grass beside the living.

nodes.label: Sarasvati
nodes.description: The great river as a goddess, best of rivers and best of mothers, who also comes to stand for inspired and eloquent speech.

nodes.label: Aditi
nodes.description: The goddess whose name means boundlessness, invoked for release from constraint and named as the mother of the Adityas.

nodes.label: Rudra
nodes.description: The feared archer of the wilds, father of the Maruts, whose arrows bring affliction on men and cattle and who is at the same time called the best of physicians.

nodes.label: Mitra
nodes.description: The god of the binding contract and of alliance, who together with Varuna upholds the ordinances and makes men keep their agreements.

nodes.label: Vayu
nodes.description: The wind as a god, called first to the pressed soma and drawn by his team through the midspace.

nodes.label: Visnu
nodes.description: The wide-strider who measures out the spaces in three steps, the third of which passes beyond where mortals can follow.

nodes.label: Mitra and Varuna
nodes.description: The sovereign pair, invoked together as the joint keepers of the ordinances and of the truth.

nodes.label: Heaven and Earth
nodes.description: The dual pair Heaven-and-Earth, invoked together as a single parental deity.

nodes.label: Tvastr
nodes.description: The divine craftsman who fashions forms and shapes the vajra for Indra, and who is invoked for the granting of offspring.

nodes.label: Indra and Agni
nodes.description: The dual of Indra and Agni, one of the most frequently invoked pairs in the corpus.

nodes.label: sacrifice (yajña)
nodes.description: The sacrificial rite itself, the act of worship offered to the gods with fire, speech and oblation.

nodes.label: the Rbhus
nodes.description: The three craftsmen who won immortality by their skill, having made the chariot of the Asvins, the bay horses of Indra and a cow from a hide.

nodes.label: Yama
nodes.description: The first mortal to die and so the first to find the path, who now rules the assembly of the Fathers and receives the newly dead.

nodes.label: Vac, Speech
nodes.description: Speech as a goddess, who declares in her own voice that she moves with all the gods and that whoever she loves becomes mighty.

nodes.label: consumption (yakṣma)
nodes.description: Yakṣma: the wasting, consuming sickness that is drawn out of a patient limb by limb in the Atharvaveda's ejection charms and flies away like a bird. Not fever, which is takman, and not affliction in general, which is amīvā.

nodes.label: soma pressing (savana)
nodes.description: The act and occasion of pressing out the soma, the rite around which most of the Rigvedic liturgy is organised.

nodes.label: plants (oṣadhi)
nodes.description: Herbs and plants, addressed collectively and chiefly as healers.

nodes.label: soma cup drawing (graha)
nodes.description: The drawing and dedication of the soma draughts, cup by cup and deity by deity: the act the Vajasaneyi Samhita's seventh and eighth adhyayas are the formulary for, whose spoken words are "upayāmagṛhīto 'si" -- thou art taken with a support -- fifty-one times, all of them Yajurvedic. Distinct from the pressing, which is VG:CONCEPT:SOMA-PRESSING: VS 18.21 inventories the pressing gear and VS 18.19-20 inventories the twenty-four drawn cups, and the corpus keeps the two lists apart.

nodes.label: the healing plants
nodes.description: The medicinal herbs, addressed collectively as mothers and goddesses who drive out disease.

nodes.label: sautramani rite (sautrāmaṇī)
nodes.description: The rite in which sura, the fermented liquor, is offered beside the soma. Named twice in the four Samhitas -- VS 19.31, "all this he gains, when juice is shed, in the Sautramani sacrifice", and AVS 3.3.2, Whitney's "with the sāutrāmaṇī́ (ceremony)" -- and supplied with its materials by VS 19-21, which name the liquor, the ram, the jujube, the young shoots and the milk in one verse.

nodes.label: the serpent
nodes.description: The serpent named as the subject of the verse.

nodes.label: Manyu, battle-fury
nodes.description: Wrath or battle-fury, addressed in the Atharvavedic hymns as a war god in his own right.

nodes.label: Parjanya
nodes.description: The rain cloud as a god, who thunders, sheds the rain and quickens the plants and the seed.

nodes.label: Nirrti, dissolution
nodes.description: The goddess of dissolution and misfortune, associated with the region below and away from the world of the living.

nodes.label: priest (hotṛ)
nodes.description: The officiant who invokes and offers, named by office rather than as an individual.

nodes.label: the rivers
nodes.description: The rivers, addressed as a collective in the dialogue with the poet who asks them to be fordable.

nodes.label: river (sindhu)
nodes.description: A flowing river, named generically; the specific named rivers stay in the place layer rather than here.

nodes.label: horse sacrifice (aśvamedha)
nodes.description: The immolation of the horse, whose formulary is VS 22-25: the horse addressed by every one of its names and consecrated "for the sacrifice" (VS 22.19), told to prepare its own body (VS 23.15), and finally apportioned part by part (VS 25.1, VS 25.41). The compound itself occurs once, at VS 18.22, where elision of the initial a- spells it `'śvamedhaś ca me` and is why an earlier pass recorded it as absent.

nodes.label: Indra and Vayu
nodes.description: The dual of Indra and Vayu, the champion and the wind.

nodes.label: Ratri, Night
nodes.description: Night as a goddess, who fills the wide spaces with darkness and stars and is asked to pass harmlessly by.

nodes.label: soma juice (soma)
nodes.description: The pressed plant and the juice made from it, drunk by the gods and by the sacrificer; the substance, not the deity of the same name.

nodes.label: Soma Pavamana
nodes.description: Soma in the act of being purified through the woollen filter, the addressee of the whole Pavamana cycle and the third most frequent devata in the corpus.

nodes.label: weapon (āyudha)
nodes.description: Weapons generally: bow, arrow and the gear a warrior or a god is armed with.

nodes.label: Visvakarman
nodes.description: The All-maker, the architect of the cosmos who names the worlds and offers up the whole of creation.

nodes.label: Agni and the Maruts
nodes.description: Agni invoked jointly with the Marut troop.

nodes.label: Indra and Brahmanaspati
nodes.description: The dual of Indra and the Lord of the sacred formulation.

nodes.label: Indra and Brhaspati
nodes.description: The dual of Indra and Brhaspati, the champion and the divine priest.

nodes.label: Purusa, the cosmic Person
nodes.description: The thousand-headed Person who is dismembered in the primal sacrifice and from whose body the worlds, the creatures and the social orders are made.

nodes.label: Agni the slayer of demons
nodes.description: Agni under the epithet rakso-han, who burns away the demons that would spoil the offering.

nodes.label: Soma and Varuna
nodes.description: The dual of Soma and Varuna.

nodes.label: Vanaspati
nodes.description: The Lord of the Forest, that is the tree and the sacrificial post cut from it, a fixed member of the apri sequence.

nodes.label: the destruction of consumption
nodes.description: A charm label: the driving out of the wasting disease yaksma.

nodes.label: livestock (paśu)
nodes.description: Domestic animals taken together, the standing measure of a household's substance.

nodes.label: fire (agni)
nodes.description: Fire as the ritual and natural phenomenon: the flame kindled on the altar and the burning that consumes, warms and carries. NOT the deity Agni, which is VG:DEVATA:AGNIH.

nodes.label: waters (āpaḥ)
nodes.description: The waters as a plural collective: rivers, rain and the primeval flood, invoked as mothers and as healers.

nodes.label: people (jana)
nodes.description: The people as a body: the clan, the tribe, the settled folk on whose behalf the rite is performed.

nodes.label: oblation (havis)
nodes.description: What is poured or placed in the fire for the gods, considered as the offered material rather than as the rite.

nodes.label: tree (vanaspati)
nodes.description: Trees and the wood taken from them, including the sacrificial post and the forest as a place.

nodes.label: fire altar piling (citi)
nodes.description: The piling up of Agni out of bricks, named by the Samhita as an act and not by a rite-name: Agni is addressed as `cīyamānaḥ`, "while thou art being piled" (VS 13.41, VS 13.47), the sacrificer as `cinvānaḥ`, "piling" (VS 13.47 and four parallels), and the bricks are addressed as bricks and called milch-cows at VS 17.2. The name `agnicayana` is absent from all four Samhitas and is not used here. `cinvānas` is read evidence but not an alias: it occurs only across a token boundary (`cinvānas tanvo`), and SANDHI_MATCH_VEDAS restricts the production substring pass to the Samaveda, so the string would fire nowhere.

nodes.label: fire oblation (agnihotra)
nodes.description: The offering poured into the fire, named as such exactly once in the four Saṃhitās (AVS 11.7.9, beside faith, the vaṣaṭ-call and the vow).

nodes.label: Brahmanaspati
nodes.description: The Lord of the sacred formulation, the divine embodiment of priestly utterance.

nodes.label: Agni, Mitra-Varuna, Ratri and Savitr
nodes.description: A four-way composite naming Agni, the Mitra-Varuna pair, Night and Savitr.

nodes.label: Agni and Indra
nodes.description: The dual of Agni and Indra, named in that order.

nodes.label: Agni and Soma
nodes.description: The dual of Agni and Soma, the fire and the pressed draught.

nodes.label: Aranyani
nodes.description: The goddess of the wild forest, praised in the single hymn addressed to her.

nodes.label: the two divine Hotrs
nodes.description: The pair of divine invoking priests, a fixed member of the apri sequence.

nodes.label: the two divine Hotrs
nodes.description: A variant label for the pair of divine invoking priests.

nodes.label: the matter in the form of implanting an embryo
nodes.description: A charm label naming conception as the subject of the verse.

nodes.label: Indra and the Maruts
nodes.description: Indra invoked jointly with the Marut troop who ride with him.

nodes.label: Indra and Pusan
nodes.description: The dual of Indra and Pusan, the champion and the guardian of the roads and herds.

nodes.label: Indra and Soma
nodes.description: The dual of Indra and Soma, the drinker and the draught.

nodes.label: Agni Jatavedas
nodes.description: Agni under the epithet Jatavedas, the knower of all that is born.

nodes.label: Indra accompanied by the Maruts
nodes.description: Indra under the epithet marutvan, the one attended by the Marut troop.

nodes.label: Agni Pavamana
nodes.description: Agni named with the clarifying participle that normally belongs to soma.

nodes.label: Soma and Pusan
nodes.description: The dual of Soma and Pusan.

nodes.label: Soma and Rudra
nodes.description: The dual of Soma and Rudra, invoked together for healing and for release from affliction.

nodes.label: horse (aśva)
nodes.description: The horse as draught animal, racer and sacrificial victim.

nodes.label: serpent (ahi)
nodes.description: The snake, both the animal charmed against in the Atharvaveda and the dragon Indra kills.

nodes.label: lifespan (āyus)
nodes.description: The span of life granted or asked for, counted in autumns rather than lived as an abstraction.

nodes.label: food (anna)
nodes.description: Food as sustenance and as what the gods are given, distinct from the oblation offered in the fire.

nodes.label: brahman priest (brahman)
nodes.description: The brahman as a person: the priest who holds the formulation, and the class of men who do. NOT the formulation itself, which is VG:CONCEPT:BRAHMAN-FORMULATION.

nodes.label: field (kṣetra)
nodes.description: Ploughed land and the work done on it, a small but distinct strand in the corpus.

nodes.label: adhvaryu (adhvaryu)
nodes.description: The officiant who does the physical work of the rite -- pressing, pouring, handling the vessels -- addressed in the plural as the men whose hands carry the offering.

nodes.label: potar priest (potṛ)
nodes.description: The officiant who purifies, and the cup drawn from his station. The office is named at RV 2.1.2 and RV 1.94.6 (Griffith's "Cleanser", "Purifier"), the officiant sits down as potar at RV 4.9.3, and the Potar's cup is drunk from at RV 1.15.2, RV 2.36.2, RV 2.37.2 and RV 2.37.4 and in the Atharvavedic parallels AVS 20.2.1, 20.2.4, 20.67.4 and 20.67.7. In the Rigvedic instances the potar is Agni; at VS 19.42 he is Soma the purifier, "yaḥ potā sa punātu mā".

nodes.label: bowstring (jyā)
nodes.description: The bowstring, addressed in its own right in the weapon hymns and the standing image for anything drawn taut.

nodes.label: the self of Agni
nodes.description: An aspect label: the atman, or self, of Agni taken as the subject of the verse.

nodes.label: Agni, Surya and Anila
nodes.description: A three-way composite naming the fire, the sun and the wind together.

nodes.label: Ahi Budhnya
nodes.description: The serpent of the depths, a benign figure invoked beside Apam Napat and the waters.

nodes.label: Apam Napat
nodes.description: The Child of the Waters, hymned as a radiant being who grows and shines within the waters.

nodes.label: the sacred grass
nodes.description: The strewn grass on which the gods are seated at the offering, and a fixed member of the apri sequence.

nodes.label: the sacred formulation
nodes.description: The formulated sacred utterance itself, taken as the subject of the verse.

nodes.label: the Brahmana, the Fathers, Soma, Heaven-and-Earth and Pusan
nodes.description: A long composite label naming five parties invoked together.

nodes.label: the bow
nodes.description: The bow, addressed in the hymn to the weapons of war.

nodes.label: the dispelling of bad dreams
nodes.description: A charm label: the destruction of evil dreams.

nodes.label: Indra and Parvata
nodes.description: The dual of Indra and Parvata, the mountain.

nodes.label: Indra and Varuna
nodes.description: The dual of Indra and Varuna, the champion and the sovereign keeper of the ordinances.

nodes.label: the Maruts, Rudra and Visnu
nodes.description: A composite label naming the Marut troop, Rudra and Visnu together.

nodes.label: Pathya Svasti, well-being on the road
nodes.description: Prosperity on the journey, addressed as a goddess of safe passage.

nodes.label: the rite for the Fathers
nodes.description: The funerary offering made to the ancestral dead, named as the subject of the verses.

nodes.label: Earth and the midspace
nodes.description: The earth and the intervening air, addressed together as a pair of regions.

nodes.label: the matter in the form of slaying a rival
nodes.description: A charm label: the purpose of the verse is the destruction of a rival.

nodes.label: Sasarpari, the Voice
nodes.description: A figure of inspired speech, brought to the poets and said to bring them renown.

nodes.label: Sita, the Furrow
nodes.description: The furrow of the ploughed field personified, invoked in the agricultural verses to be propitious and to yield milk and grain.

nodes.label: the blessings of well-being
nodes.description: Wishes for safety and well-being, named collectively as the subject of the verses.

nodes.label: Dawn and Night
nodes.description: The dual of Dawn and Night, the two sisters who follow one another in turn.

nodes.label: the steeds
nodes.description: The swift horses, addressed collectively as prize-winners.

nodes.label: Vac and the Waters
nodes.description: Speech and the Waters addressed jointly.

nodes.label: the armour
nodes.description: The body armour, addressed in the hymn to the weapons of war.

nodes.label: Vastospati
nodes.description: The Lord of the Dwelling, the tutelary spirit of the house, asked to grant a favourable entry and to keep sickness away.

nodes.label: the sacrificial post
nodes.description: The post to which the victim is tied, anointed and addressed as a participant in the rite.

nodes.label: cattle (go)
nodes.description: Cows and cattle, the principal wealth of the corpus and the object of the raid that several central myths retell.

nodes.label: bird (vi)
nodes.description: Birds, from the omen-bird of the Atharvaveda to the eagle that brings the soma down.

nodes.label: heaven (dyaus)
nodes.description: The sky as the upper world, father of the pair Heaven-and-Earth.

nodes.label: earth (pṛthivī)
nodes.description: The earth as the lower world and as the broad surface that bears living things.

nodes.label: speech (vāc)
nodes.description: Speech as a power: the voice that carries the hymn and, in some hymns, a cosmic agent in her own right.

nodes.label: sun (sūrya)
nodes.description: The sun as the visible luminary that crosses the sky and measures the day.

nodes.label: birth (janman)
nodes.description: Coming into being: birth, begetting and the generation of the world in the cosmogonic hymns.

nodes.label: mind (manas)
nodes.description: Mind as the seat of intention and attention, something that can go away and be called back.

nodes.label: offspring (prajā)
nodes.description: Progeny and continuity of the line, one of the two things (with cattle) most often asked for.

nodes.label: wellbeing (svasti)
nodes.description: Being well and getting through safely; the closing wish of a great many hymns.

nodes.label: protection (śarman)
nodes.description: Shelter and defence asked of a god, the covering under which a household is safe.

nodes.label: clarified butter (ghṛta)
nodes.description: Melted butter, the commonest liquid oblation and a standing image for anything rich, streaming or nourishing.

nodes.label: dawn (uṣas)
nodes.description: Daybreak, and the recurring arrival of light that the hymns treat as a daily renewal of the world.

nodes.label: sacred grass (barhis)
nodes.description: The strewn grass on which the gods are invited to sit at the sacrifice.

nodes.label: world (loka)
nodes.description: A world or region of space, including the free room a person is asked to be given.

nodes.label: stone (grāvan)
nodes.description: Stone as a substance and as ritual equipment: the pressing stones that crush the soma stalks, and stone generally as the hard thing a god splits or a press works with.

nodes.label: milk (payas)
nodes.description: Milk, both the cow's and the figurative milk of clouds, plants and the earth.

nodes.label: death (mṛtyu)
nodes.description: Death as an event and as a power that binds, chiefly something to be kept away.

nodes.label: sacrificer (yajamāna)
nodes.description: The man on whose behalf and at whose cost the rite is performed: not an officiant, and the party most of the corpus's requests are made for.

nodes.label: cup (camasa)
nodes.description: The drinking cup of the sacrifice, the one the Ṛbhus made fourfold and the one the gods are asked to drink from.

nodes.label: midday pressing (mādhyandina savana)
nodes.description: The second of the day's three soma pressings, named by its time of day at RV 3.28.4, RV 3.32.3, RV 5.40.4, AVS 7.76.6 and AVS 20.12.7, and by its ordinal at AVS 6.47.2 -- "asmin dvitīye savane", "at this second libation". VS 19.26 assigns it to Indra.

nodes.label: mortar (ulūkhala)
nodes.description: The wooden mortar and its pestle, the household pair that pounds grain and presses soma and is addressed as a divinity in RV 1.28.

nodes.label: sacrificial post (yūpa)
nodes.description: The post to which the animal victim is tied, and the svaru splinter cut from it that is offered with the victim.

nodes.label: nestar priest (neṣṭṛ)
nodes.description: The officiant who leads or conducts, Griffith's "Leader", and the cup drawn from his station. The office at RV 2.1.2 and RV 10.91.10 ("tava neṣṭraṃ"), the cup at RV 1.15.9, RV 2.37.3 and RV 2.37.4, and in the Vajasaneyi Samhita at VS 26.22, "neṣṭrād ṛtubhir iṣyata".

nodes.label: directing priest (praśāstṛ)
nodes.description: The officiant who directs the rite, Griffith's "Director". Named as an agent at RV 1.94.6 ("praśāstā potā januṣā purohitaḥ") and RV 2.5.4 ("as Director was he born"), and as an office at RV 2.1.2 and RV 10.91.10 ("tava praśāstraṃ"). Agni holds it in all four.

nodes.label: wooden soma tub (droṇakalaśa)
nodes.description: The trough-shaped wooden vessel the pressed soma is collected in. Named in the apparatus inventory at VS 18.21, gained by the Vayu cups at VS 19.27, and listed with the kettles and the drinking-vessels at AVS 9.6.17. The VS 18.21 attestation is read evidence but not an alias: there the word sits inside `droṇakalaśaśca`, reachable only by the substring pass, which production runs on the Samaveda alone.

nodes.label: Sarasvati river (sarasvatī)
nodes.description: The Sarasvatī as a place on the ground, on the only two occasions in the four Saṃhitās where the grammar says so: the barley the gods ploughed on it (AVS 6.30.1) and the rivers Agni is asked to shine on (RV 3.23.4). The goddess is VG:DEVATA:SARASVATI and is not this node; the river hymns belong to her, because their case forms do not distinguish the two.

nodes.label: vayu cup (vāyavya)
nodes.description: The cups belonging to Vayu, drawn in the soma rite. Two attestations, in two Vedas, both read: "camasāś ca me vāyavyāni ca me" in the apparatus inventory at VS 18.21, and Whitney's "the drinking-vessels those of Vāyu" at AVS 9.6.17. The bare stem `vāyavya` is refused: one of its three substring hits is `sakthyor vāyavyaḥ`, an anatomical term inside the horse's dismemberment.

nodes.label: the All-Gods
nodes.description: The gods invoked as a single collective addressee, the fourth most frequent devata in the corpus.

nodes.label: the curse
nodes.description: A curse, or the imputation of guilt, named as the subject of the verse.

nodes.label: the Adityas and the Dawns
nodes.description: A composite label naming the Aditya gods together with the dawns.

nodes.label: Agni and the Maruts (agnāmarutaḥ)
nodes.description: A variant source label pairing Agni with the Maruts, printed as a solid dvandva on the stem agna- rather than as the editors' hyphenated pair.

nodes.label: Agni and Surya
nodes.description: A dual label pairing Agni with the sun.

nodes.label: food
nodes.description: Food itself praised as the subject of the verse.

nodes.label: the two bow-tips
nodes.description: The two ends of the bow where the string is fastened, addressed in the weapons hymn.

nodes.label: the horses
nodes.description: The horses addressed collectively as the subject of the verse.

nodes.label: the horse
nodes.description: The sacrificial horse, addressed as the victim of the horse rite.

nodes.label: the self
nodes.description: The self or breath-soul, named as the subject of the verse.

nodes.label: the returning mind
nodes.description: A charm label: the calling back of a mind that has strayed or departed.

nodes.label: the course of becoming
nodes.description: A cosmogonic theme label: the coming-to-be of things.

nodes.label: the course of becoming
nodes.description: An orthographic variant of the bhavavrtta theme label.

nodes.label: the Moon
nodes.description: The moon as a celestial body, taken as the subject of the verse.

nodes.label: Dadhikra
nodes.description: The divine racehorse, praised at daybreak alongside Usas and the Asvins.

nodes.label: Dadhikra
nodes.description: A variant source label for the divine racehorse Dadhikra.

nodes.label: Daksina, the priestly fee
nodes.description: The sacrificial fee or largesse, addressed as a giving power in her own right.

nodes.label: the divine doors
nodes.description: The doors of the sacrificial enclosure, a fixed member of the apri sequence.

nodes.label: Dhatr
nodes.description: The Establisher, a late-Vedic ordaining god whose name is the agent noun for the one who sets things in place.

nodes.label: the bestower of goods
nodes.description: An epithet standing as a deity name in its own right, the giver of wealth.

nodes.label: the war drum
nodes.description: The battle drum, addressed as a power that routs the enemy.

nodes.label: Heaven and Earth (dyāvābhūmī)
nodes.description: The dual pair Heaven-and-Earth, in the bhumi variant of the name.

nodes.label: Heaven, Earth and the Asvins
nodes.description: A composite label naming heaven, earth and the Asvin twins together.

nodes.label: the cow
nodes.description: The cow, praised as a being in her own right.

nodes.label: the pressing stones
nodes.description: The stones that crush the soma stalks, addressed as a speaking collective.

nodes.label: Ila, Sarasvati and Mahi
nodes.description: The three goddesses invoked together in the apri sequence, associated with nourishment and with inspired speech.

nodes.label: Indra and Visnu
nodes.description: The dual of Indra and Visnu.

nodes.label: Indra and Usas
nodes.description: The dual of Indra and the Dawn.

nodes.label: the arrows
nodes.description: The arrows, addressed in the hymn to the weapons of war.

nodes.label: the quiver
nodes.description: The quiver, addressed in the hymn to the weapons of war.

nodes.label: knowledge
nodes.description: Knowledge itself, named as the subject of the verse.

nodes.label: the bowstring
nodes.description: The bowstring, addressed in the hymn to the weapons of war.

nodes.label: Ka, the Who
nodes.description: The interrogative pronoun who, standing as a deity name in the cosmogonic hymn that asks to which god the oblation should be offered.

nodes.label: ploughing
nodes.description: Agriculture itself, named as the subject of the agricultural verses.

nodes.label: Ksetrapati
nodes.description: The Lord of the Field, invoked in the agricultural verses for a good yield of crops and cattle.

nodes.label: the frogs
nodes.description: The frogs whose croaking at the first rains is compared to priests chanting.

nodes.label: the piercing of illusion
nodes.description: The breaking through of maya, deceptive appearance, named as the theme of the verse.

nodes.label: Death
nodes.description: Death itself, addressed in the funeral verses as a power to be sent away along its own separate path.

nodes.label: the Panis
nodes.description: The niggardly ones who hoard the cows and refuse the sacrifice, the adversaries in the dialogue with Sarama.

nodes.label: Pavamana, the one being clarified
nodes.description: The soma in the act of being strained, named by that participle alone without the word soma.

nodes.label: the chariot
nodes.description: The war chariot, addressed as a power in the verses on the gear of battle.

nodes.label: the parts of the chariot
nodes.description: The components of the chariot, addressed collectively.

nodes.label: the granting, or delight
nodes.description: An abstract noun covering both giving and pleasure, named as the subject of the verse.

nodes.label: the bird
nodes.description: The bird whose call is read as an omen and which is asked to speak only what is auspicious.

nodes.label: concord
nodes.description: Agreement of mind, the theme of the closing verses that ask the assembly to think as one.

nodes.label: the matter in the form of subduing a co-wife
nodes.description: A charm label: the purpose of the verse is the suppression of a rival wife.

nodes.label: the two dogs of Sarama
nodes.description: The two four-eyed dogs, sons of Sarama, who guard the road to Yama and are asked to let the dead pass safely.

nodes.label: Sarasvati, Ila and Bharati
nodes.description: The triad of goddesses invoked together in the apri sequence, in the ordering that names Bharati third.

nodes.label: Surya, daughter of Savitr
nodes.description: The feminine Surya, the Sun-maiden, whose marriage procession is described in the long wedding hymn.

nodes.label: Soma and the Sun
nodes.description: A dual pairing the soma draught with arka, the sun or the ray.

nodes.label: Sraddha, Faith
nodes.description: Faith or trust addressed as a goddess, invoked at morning, noon and sunset to be placed in the worshipper.

nodes.label: the reviving of Subandhu
nodes.description: The restoration to life of the man Subandhu, named as the purpose of the verses.

nodes.label: Suna and Sira
nodes.description: The paired deities of the ploughshare and the plough, invoked in the agricultural verses for a good crop.

nodes.label: the wedding of Surya
nodes.description: The marriage of the Sun-maiden, named as the event the verses narrate.

nodes.label: the svaha calls
nodes.description: The ritual exclamations svaha that accompany the pouring of the oblation.

nodes.label: the falcon
nodes.description: The falcon that carried the soma down from heaven, named as the subject of the verse.

nodes.label: Tarksya
nodes.description: A divine swift being, described as a horse or a bird of victory and invoked for speed and success.

nodes.label: the mortar
nodes.description: The wooden mortar in which the soma stalks are pounded, addressed as an agent of the rite.

nodes.label: the mortar and pestle
nodes.description: The mortar together with the pestle, addressed as a working pair.

nodes.label: the All-Gods
nodes.description: A source-spelling variant of the All-Gods collective, written with a retroflex sibilant.

nodes.label: the sacrifice and the sacrificer
nodes.description: The rite together with the man who commissions it, addressed as a dual.

nodes.label: wealth (rayi)
nodes.description: Goods and riches asked for from the gods, counted in cattle, horses, gold and heroes rather than in money.

nodes.label: sacred formulation (brahman)
nodes.description: The formulated sacred utterance and the power in it, before the word acquired its later Upanishadic sense.

nodes.label: chariot (ratha)
nodes.description: The chariot, the vehicle of gods and warriors and the standing image for a well-made hymn.

nodes.label: insight (dhī)
nodes.description: Visionary thought, the poet's insight that produces the hymn rather than ordinary reasoning.

nodes.label: wind (vāta)
nodes.description: The wind as a moving natural force, blowing, healing and driving the clouds.

nodes.label: thunderbolt (vajra)
nodes.description: The bolt, Indra's weapon, treated as a distinct object rather than as lightning.

nodes.label: enemy (śatru)
nodes.description: The human adversary: rival, hostile tribe, or the Dasa and Dasyu the hymns set against the sacrificer.

nodes.label: ancestors (pitaraḥ)
nodes.description: The dead forefathers as a class, receiving their own offerings and their own hymns.

nodes.label: midspace (antarikṣa)
nodes.description: The space between heaven and earth, where wind, cloud and the Maruts move.

nodes.label: demon (rakṣas)
nodes.description: The non-human hostile being -- rakshas, yatudhana, pishacha -- against whom whole Atharvavedic hymns are directed.

nodes.label: honey (madhu)
nodes.description: Honey, and the honeyed quality attributed to soma, milk and speech alike.

nodes.label: strainer (pavitra)
nodes.description: The woollen filter through which the pressed soma is strained clean, and the purifying it performs.

nodes.label: overcoming rivals (sapatna)
nodes.description: The wish to put down a rival -- a competitor for rank, a rival claimant, a co-wife -- as distinct from defeating an enemy in war.

nodes.label: kindling (samidh)
nodes.description: The wood with which the sacrificial fire is kindled, and the state of being kindled.

nodes.label: priestly fee (dakṣiṇā)
nodes.description: The fee paid to the officiants, treated in the hymns as itself a meritorious act.

nodes.label: rain (vṛṣṭi)
nodes.description: Rainfall, asked for as the release of the waters held in the sky.

nodes.label: jar (kalaśa)
nodes.description: The jar or pitcher into which the pressed soma runs and out of which it is drunk; the commonest vessel of Mandala 9.

nodes.label: darbha grass (darbha)
nodes.description: Darbha grass, addressed in its own hymns as an amulet that splits the heart of a rival; not the strewn barhis of the sacrifice.

nodes.label: lightning (vidyut)
nodes.description: Lightning and thunder, the audible and visible violence of the storm.

nodes.label: hereditary disease (kṣetriya)
nodes.description: The inherited or field-borne affliction, a disease category with no counterpart outside the Atharvaveda.

nodes.label: household priest (purohita)
nodes.description: The priest "placed in front" of a household or a king, an office the corpus attributes to men and to Agni in the same words.

nodes.label: kushtha (kuṣṭha)
nodes.description: Kushtha, a herb said to come down from the Himalaya, used against fever.

nodes.label: altar (vedi)
nodes.description: The excavated altar ground on which the grass is strewn and the offering set; in RV 1.164.35 the earth's own outermost limit.

nodes.label: jangida (jaṅgiḍa)
nodes.description: Jangida, worn as an amulet against viskandha and other seizing afflictions.

nodes.label: ashvattha (aśvattha)
nodes.description: The aśvatthá, the holy fig: born out of the khadira and told to crush the speaker's foes in AVS 3.6 and 8.8, named as the seat of the gods in the third heaven where they won the kuṣṭha, and the home of the herbs at RV 10.97.5.

nodes.label: balasa (balāsa)
nodes.description: A named Atharvavedic sickness of the joints and limbs, left untranslated here because the corpus describes its treatment and not its symptoms.

nodes.label: offering ladle (sruc)
nodes.description: The offering ladle and spoon -- sruc, sruva -- with which butter is lifted and poured into the fire.

nodes.label: funerary rites (pitṛyāṇa)
nodes.description: The disposal of the dead and the road they take: the cremation ground and the fathers' path, as against the ancestors themselves.

nodes.label: apamarga (apāmārga)
nodes.description: Apamarga, "the wiper-off", the plant of the counter-witchcraft hymns.

nodes.label: arundhati (arundhatī)
nodes.description: Arundhati, a climbing herb invoked for the healing of fractures and wounds.

nodes.label: jaundice (hariman)
nodes.description: The yellow sickness, treated by transferring the patient's yellowness to yellow birds and taking the red of a bull in exchange.

nodes.label: khadira (khadira)
nodes.description: The khadirá, the hard-wooded acacia: the tree the aśvattha is born from, the wood of an amulet in AVS 10.6, one of the six trees the healing plant of AVS 5.5 arises from, and the timber a chariot axle is asked to be firm as at RV 3.53.19.

nodes.label: axe (svadhiti)
nodes.description: The axe or hatchet: the tool that fells the tree and the blade that jointed the sacrificial horse.

nodes.label: morning pressing (prātaḥsavana)
nodes.description: The first of the day's three soma pressings, named by its time of day. RV 3.28.1 and RV 3.52.4 offer the cake "prātaḥsāve"; AVS 6.47.1 has Agni protect us "prātaḥsavane"; and RV 10.112.1 calls it the first draught outright -- "prātaḥsāvas tava hi pūrvapītiḥ", Griffith's "thy first draught is early morn's libation".

nodes.label: gulgulu (gulgulu)
nodes.description: Gulgulu, the aromatic resin (later guggulu) named among the substances whose smell drives sickness off.

nodes.label: leprous spot (kilāsa)
nodes.description: The white or pale skin patch, treated by a night-born dark herb told to give the skin back its own colour; the corpus distinguishes the bone-born from the body-born kind and from the kind "made by the spoiler".

nodes.label: prshniparni (pṛśniparṇī)
nodes.description: The spotted-leaf, "weal for us, woe for Nirṛti": a grinder-up of the kaṇvas and a hewer of the heads of the ill-named ones, invoked against the embryo-eating demon.

nodes.label: fire kindler (agnīdh)
nodes.description: The officiant who kindles the fire. Two attestations, in two Vedas, and both were read: RV 2.1.2 and RV 10.91.10, where Agni is told "tvam agnid ṛtāyataḥ" (Griffith's "Kindler for the pious man"), and VS 7.15, where the kindler is addressed in the vocative at the close of the offering formula, `yāḍ agnīt`. The stems `agnīdh` and `agnīdhraḥ` match nothing anywhere in the corpus.

nodes.label: laksha (lākṣā)
nodes.description: The healing plant of AVS 5.5, which that hymn names twice over -- silācī́ in verses 1 and 8, lā́kṣā in verse 7 -- and which it addresses alongside arundhatī for the closing of wounds. Two names for one addressee, so one entity, on the hymn's own authority rather than on a botanical identification.

nodes.label: Parushni (paruṣṇī)
nodes.description: The Paruṣṇī, the river of the battle of ten kings, and in AVS 6.12 one of the streams said to run with honey.

nodes.label: ajashringi (ajaśṛṅgī)
nodes.description: The goat-horned plant, also called arāṭakī́, whose smell is said to expel the Apsarases and Gandharvas in AVS 4.37.

nodes.label: heart-burn (hṛddyota)
nodes.description: Burning of the heart, sent up to the sun together with yellowness in the jaundice hymn, and the thing the heavenly waters are asked for a remedy for at AVS 6.24.

nodes.label: honey-plant (madugha)
nodes.description: The madúgha or honey-plant, named in the Atharvaveda's two love charms only: once as the thing the speaker claims to be sweeter than, once among the substances that make up a means of subjection.

nodes.label: pippali (pippalī)
nodes.description: The pippalī berry, called in its own hymn a remedy for what is bruised and for what is pierced, and made by the gods sufficient for life. Kept apart from pippalá, the sweet berry of the two eagles on the cosmic tree.

nodes.label: Sarayu (sarayu)
nodes.description: The Sarayu, named among the waters that might hold a traveller back.

nodes.label: Vipash (vipāś)
nodes.description: The Vipāś, one of the two rivers Viśvāmitra addresses and asks to be forded in RV 3.33.

nodes.label: Yamuna (yamunā)
nodes.description: The Yamunā, named in the river litany of RV 10.75 and among the allies of the Tṛtsus in RV 7.18.

nodes.label: hemp (bhaṅga)
nodes.description: Hemp, named once, in the list of the five kingdoms of plants at AVS 11.6.15 -- darbhá, hemp, barley and sáha -- asked together to free the speaker from distress. One occurrence, and the reason the bare stem is not an alias is that bhaṅg- is otherwise the root "to break".

nodes.label: Ganges (gaṅgā)
nodes.description: The Ganges, named once in the river litany of RV 10.75 and nowhere else in the four Saṃhitās.

nodes.label: ritual brick (iṣṭakā)
nodes.description: The brick the fire is piled out of, addressed directly and only in the Yajurveda: "imā me agna iṣṭakā dhenavaḥ santu", let these bricks of mine, Agni, be milch-cows (VS 17.2). Token-matched once and read once; its four substring hits are 40% intrusions and are not relied on.

nodes.label: Shutudri (śutudrī)
nodes.description: The Śutudrī, the Vipāś's companion in RV 3.33 and a name in the litany of RV 10.75.

nodes.label: third pressing (tṛtīya savana)
nodes.description: The third of the day's three soma pressings, and the one the corpus numbers most often: "tṛtīye savane" at RV 3.28.5, "idaṃ tṛtīyaṃ savanaṃ kavīnām" at AVS 6.47.3, "tṛtīye savana ṛbhūṇām" at AVS 9.1.13, and the Rbhus' third libation at RV 4.34.4, RV 4.35.9 and RV 8.57.1. All six were read and all six are this act -- and none of them is reachable, because the third pressing is the only one of the three the corpus never writes as one word. The morning has prātaḥsāva and the midday has mādhyaṃdina; the third has only the phrase tṛtīya + savana, and SANDHI_MATCH_VEDAS restricts the production substring pass to the Samaveda. The one alias is therefore VS 19.26's single token, `tṛtīyamāptaṃṃ`, whose doubled anusvara is an artefact of this corpus's VSM transliteration and is recorded as such in the report: it is brittle by construction and will need replacing if that transliteration is normalised.

nodes.label: chanter priest (udgātṛ)
nodes.description: The priest who chants the Saman. Named exactly once in the four Samhitas, and in a simile: at RV 2.43.2 a bird is told "udgāteva śakune sāma gāyasi", "thou like the chanter-priest chantest the Sama". The Rigveda's manual annotation confirms the form as udgātár-, nominative singular masculine. The office does not occur in the Samaveda, whose chant it exists to sing.

nodes.label: vishanaka (viṣāṇakā)
nodes.description: "Horny" by name, called Rudra's urine and the navel of the immortal, and declared in its single occurrence to be an effacer of the wind-caused ailment.

nodes.label: praise of the reciter
nodes.description: Praise of the one who recites or studies the text, rather than of any deity.

nodes.label: the dice
nodes.description: The dice of the gambler hymn, addressed collectively as a power over the player.

nodes.label: censure of the dice and the gambler
nodes.description: The reproach of dice and of the gambler, the theme of the gambler hymn.

nodes.label: the dispelling of ill fortune
nodes.description: A charm label: the driving away of alaksmi, bad fortune.

nodes.label: Surya, with the epithet aptrna
nodes.description: A Surya label carrying the obscure qualifier aptrna.

nodes.label: the conducting of the life-breath
nodes.description: The leading onward of the asu, the life-breath, after death.

nodes.label: the hands of Bandhu and the others
nodes.description: A phrase label naming the hands of the rishi Bandhu and his companions.

nodes.label: the married pair
nodes.description: Husband and wife addressed together as a dual.

nodes.label: the blessings of the married pair
nodes.description: The wishes or benedictions of husband and wife.

nodes.label: the gods
nodes.description: The gods addressed as an undifferentiated collective.

nodes.label: the wives of the gods
nodes.description: The consorts of the gods, invoked as a collective.

nodes.label: the goddesses
nodes.description: The goddesses addressed as an undifferentiated collective.

nodes.label: the tawny one
nodes.description: A label meaning the tawny or bay one, used as a deity name.

nodes.label: the archer's hand-guard
nodes.description: The guard protecting the archer's forearm from the bowstring, addressed in the weapons hymn.

nodes.label: the two oblation carts
nodes.description: The pair of carts that carry the soma and the oblations to the offering ground.

nodes.label: the benedictions of the Hotr
nodes.description: The blessings uttered by the invoking priest.

nodes.label: Indrani, Varunani and Agnayi
nodes.description: The three consort goddesses named from Indra, Varuna and Agni.

nodes.label: the two horses of Indra
nodes.description: The pair of bay steeds belonging to Indra, addressed as the subject.

nodes.label: the deities indicated by the wording
nodes.description: An Anukramani bookkeeping label meaning that the deity is whichever one the verse itself names.

nodes.label: the goad
nodes.description: The driver's goad, addressed in the hymn to the weapons and gear of the chariot.

nodes.label: Raka
nodes.description: The goddess of the night of the full moon, invoked with the other goddesses of the lunar days for offspring and wealth.

nodes.label: the guardian of the chariot
nodes.description: The protector of the war chariot, addressed in the verses on the gear of battle.

nodes.label: Rnancaya and Indra
nodes.description: A dual joining the patron Rnancaya with Indra.

nodes.label: Saci, might
nodes.description: Might or effective power, standing as the subject of the verse.

nodes.label: the Sadhyas
nodes.description: A class of ancient divine beings named as having performed the sacrifice in the earliest time.

nodes.label: the wheel of the year
nodes.description: The turning year as a wheel of time, the theme of the riddle verses on the twelve-spoked wheel.

nodes.label: Sarama
nodes.description: The divine bitch sent by Indra as his envoy to the Panis, who finds the hidden cows and refuses their bribe.

nodes.label: Saranyu
nodes.description: The daughter of Tvastr, named in the genealogical verses as a mother of divine twins.

nodes.label: Sarasvan
nodes.description: The masculine counterpart of Sarasvati, invoked in a small number of verses.

nodes.label: the charioteer and the reins
nodes.description: The driver of the chariot together with the reins he holds, addressed jointly.

nodes.label: Sinivali
nodes.description: The goddess of the night of the new moon, invoked with the other goddesses of the lunar days for offspring.

nodes.label: Urvasi
nodes.description: The nymph who has lived among mortals and is departing, the speaker opposite Pururavas in the dialogue hymn.

nodes.label: Vena
nodes.description: An obscure luminous figure of the higher regions, described in a single difficult hymn in terms drawn from the Gandharvas and the waters.

nodes.label: the wedding verses
nodes.description: The mantras recited at a marriage, named as the subject of the passage.

nodes.label: Yami
nodes.description: The twin sister of Yama, who argues with him for union and is refused in the dialogue hymn.

nodes.label: bull (vṛṣabha)
nodes.description: The bull and the draught ox: the animal itself, and the same word used of a god whose strength is being praised, which the corpus does not distinguish.

nodes.label: sheep (avi)
nodes.description: Sheep, ewe and ram, and the fleece taken from them -- which is why this concept reaches Mandala 9, where the soma runs through a filter of sheep's wool.

nodes.label: goat (aja)
nodes.description: The goat: the victim led before the horse at the horse sacrifice, the animal cooked with five rice-dishes, and a head of ordinary livestock.

nodes.label: adder (pṛdāku)
nodes.description: The pṛ́dāku, a named venomous snake of the Atharvaveda's snake charms, listed beside the cross-lined one, the black snake and the kasarṇī́la, and once set as the guardian of the western quarter. Every occurrence is Atharvavedic.

nodes.label: frog (maṇḍūka)
nodes.description: The frog, whose croaking at the first rains is a whole hymn (RV 7.103) and a Yajurvedic sacrificial animal.

nodes.label: dog (śvan)
nodes.description: The dog: the household animal that is told to sleep in the two burglary charms, the hound that wakes the Ṛbhus, and one of the hundred gifts of a patron.

nodes.label: constrictor (svaja)
nodes.description: The svajá, the snake that coils, named in AVS 10.4 as one of the two things the young physician grinds up. Kept apart from the imperative of svaj- "to embrace", which is the same string at AVS 5.14.10 and 12.3.12.

nodes.label: cosmic order (ṛta)
nodes.description: The right ordering of the world, of the seasons and of the rite, which gods and men are said to follow rather than to legislate.

nodes.label: prize (vāja)
nodes.description: The prize or booty won in a contest, and by metonymy the vigour that wins it.

nodes.label: praise (stoma)
nodes.description: The act of praising a god, and the composed praise-song as an offering in its own right.

nodes.label: kingship (rājan)
nodes.description: Rule: the king, his realm and the sovereign authority attributed equally to men and to Varuna.

nodes.label: house (gṛha)
nodes.description: The dwelling as a place and as the unit whose safety the rite secures.

nodes.label: resolve (kratu)
nodes.description: Effective mental force: the capacity to form a plan and carry it out, attributed to gods and asked for by men.

nodes.label: ordinance (vrata)
nodes.description: A fixed observance or commandment, the particular rule as against the general order.

nodes.label: ocean (samudra)
nodes.description: The sea or great gathered water, also used of the vat into which pressed soma streams.

nodes.label: embryo (garbha)
nodes.description: The embryo or germ in the womb; the corpus applies the same word to the germ of fire in the waters, so this is the word's range and not only human pregnancy.

nodes.label: path (adhvan)
nodes.description: The road travelled, literal and figurative, including the paths of order the gods keep to.

nodes.label: hero (vīra)
nodes.description: The able man: the fighting son whose presence is itself counted among a household's goods.

nodes.label: chant (sāman)
nodes.description: The sung melody to which a verse is set, as distinct from the words of the verse.

nodes.label: liberality (dāna)
nodes.description: Giving as a virtue and as a transaction: the patron's gift, praised in the danastuti verses appended to many hymns.

nodes.label: healing (bheṣaja)
nodes.description: Remedy and cure, the act of making whole, overwhelmingly an Atharvavedic concern.

nodes.label: amulet (maṇi)
nodes.description: The amulet: a bead, shell, plant or metal object bound on a person and addressed as the active agent of the charm.

nodes.label: sin (enas)
nodes.description: Fault or offence incurred against gods or men, thought of as something one is loosed from rather than forgiven for.

nodes.label: wile (māyā)
nodes.description: Transformative craft, admirable in a god and treacherous in an enemy, with the same word for both.

nodes.label: night (rātri)
nodes.description: Night as a division of time and as the interval the sacrificer asks to pass safely through.

nodes.label: mountain (parvata)
nodes.description: A mountain or rock mass, including the one Indra splits to free the cows and the waters.

nodes.label: noose (pāśa)
nodes.description: The noose or snare, above all Varuṇa's and Death's: the binding weapon a hymn asks to be released from rather than one it asks to be given.

nodes.label: self (ātman)
nodes.description: The self or animating principle of a being, still concrete in this corpus and not yet the Upanishadic absolute.

nodes.label: armour (varman)
nodes.description: Armour as a worn thing, literal mail and the figurative armour an amulet or a god is said to be; the object, not the shelter asked for.

nodes.label: marriage (vivāha)
nodes.description: The wedding: the bride, the bridal procession that conveys her, and the marriage occasion itself.

nodes.label: barley (yava)
nodes.description: Barley, the one cereal the corpus names constantly: ploughed, reaped, eaten, and offered, and the crop against which hunger is measured.

nodes.label: moon (candramas)
nodes.description: The moon, named chiefly where the corpus lists the lights of the sky together.

nodes.label: faith (śraddhā)
nodes.description: Trust that the rite and the god will hold good; in RV 10.151 a power addressed in its own right.

nodes.label: house building (śālā)
nodes.description: The raising and occupation of a dwelling as a ritual act, addressed to the hut in the second person; the building, not the house as a place.

nodes.label: grain (dhānya)
nodes.description: Grain in general, and specifically the parched or roasted grain (dhānā) set out for Indra's horses and scattered for the dead.

nodes.label: evil dream (duṣvapnya)
nodes.description: The evil dream, treated as an affliction with an owner: it is dispatched to an enemy rather than merely dispelled.

nodes.label: length of life (dīrghāyutva)
nodes.description: Length of life, as the stated purpose of an act: the dative dīrghāyutvā́ya, "in order to length of life", is what an amulet is bound on for, what a patient is enclosed in red colours for, and what a husband is wished. That dative accounts for 15 of the entity's 20 token occurrences, and 14 of those 15 are Atharvavedic.

nodes.label: fermented draught (parisrut)
nodes.description: The draught that has flowed round, poured beside milk, ghee and honey in the sautramani: "payaḥ somaḥ parisrutā ghṛtaṃ madhu" (VS 21.30, VS 21.31), "somaṃ śukraṃ parisrutā sarasvatī" (VS 20.59). Eighteen passages, every one Yajurvedic and not one anywhere else in the corpus.

nodes.label: drum (dundubhi)
nodes.description: The war drum, addressed directly in the battle charms and told to roar the enemy away.

nodes.label: consecration (dīkṣā)
nodes.description: The consecration that makes a man fit to sacrifice, treated in the Atharvaveda as a power in its own right and in VS 19.30 as what a vow earns.

nodes.label: seizure (grāhi)
nodes.description: Grahi, the Seizer: a seizing sickness personified as a female power whose fetters a patient is released from.

nodes.label: childbirth (sūṣā)
nodes.description: Delivery as an occasion needing ritual help: the birth itself, the afterbirth, and the charm for causing conception.

nodes.label: Turvasha (turvaśa)
nodes.description: The Turvaśas, the Yadus' constant pair; the one tribe name of this set that the Sāmaveda also carries.

nodes.label: defence (paripāṇa)
nodes.description: Paripā́ṇa, defence round about: asked for in the bare formula "protection art thou; protection mayest thou give me: hail!" and predicated of the ointment, of the reverting amulet and of the jaṅgiḍá. Every token occurrence is Atharvavedic.

nodes.label: viskandha (viṣkandha)
nodes.description: A named Atharvavedic affliction warded off by amulets, chiefly the jangida and the thousand-powered amulet; left untranslated for the same reason as balasa.

nodes.label: Purus (pūru)
nodes.description: The Pūrus, for whom Indra breaks open forts and makes room.

nodes.label: Bharatas (bharata)
nodes.description: The Bharatas, the people for whom Agni is kindled in Mandala 3 and who ford the rivers in RV 3.33.

nodes.label: spirituous liquor (surā)
nodes.description: The fermented liquor offered beside the soma in the sautramani: "surayā somaḥ suta āsuto madāya" (VS 19.5), "somasya śuṣmaḥ surayā sutasya" (VS 19.33). Griffith renders it "Wine". The bare stem `surā` is deliberately not an alias: at four characters it is below the sandhi floor, its 116 substring hits are 47% intrusions, and three of its six token hits are the dicing-and-drinking topos of AVS 6.70.1 and RV 7.86.6 rather than an offering.

nodes.label: apacit swellings (apacit)
nodes.description: The apacíts: swellings counted off in fives, sevens and nines over the nape, neck, shoulders and sides, and told to fly away like a bird from its nest. Left untranslated beyond "swellings" because the corpus gives their sites and their colours and not their nature.

nodes.label: udumbara amulet (audumbara)
nodes.description: The amulet of udumbara wood, worn in AVS 19.31 for prosperity, cattle and fatness in the cow-stall, and addressed as prosperity itself. All seven occurrences are in that one hymn.

nodes.label: cough (kāsa)
nodes.description: Cough, listed among the ailments to be sent flying away from a patient's joints.

nodes.label: concord (saṃjñāna)
nodes.description: Agreement of mind within a household or an assembly, asked for as a positive good between kin and strangers alike.

nodes.label: Yadu (yadu)
nodes.description: The Yadus, named almost always in one breath with the Turvaśas as a distant people Indra brought or held back.

nodes.label: headache (śīrṣakti)
nodes.description: Head-pain, in the two words the corpus uses for it: śīrṣakti the ache and śīrṣāmaya the head-ailment, both expelled by incantation at AVS 9.8.1 and both wiped off onto lead and onto a pillow at AVS 12.2.

nodes.label: sesame (tila)
nodes.description: Sesame, eaten, pressed for oil, and scattered mixed with grain for the dead.

nodes.label: flux (āsrāva)
nodes.description: A flowing or discharging complaint, named in the Atharvaveda beside the plants and reeds used to stanch it.

nodes.label: jayanya (jāyānya)
nodes.description: Jāyānya, a winged sickness that "flies and enters into a man", crushes the breast-bone and descends to the sole; named beside jaundice and visalpaka as something the ointment drives out. Untranslated for the same reason as balasa.

nodes.label: visalpaka (visalpaka)
nodes.description: A named Atharvavedic ailment of the limbs, ears and eyes, ejected together with the abscess and the heart-disease; left untranslated because the corpus gives its sites and its remedy and not its nature.

nodes.label: Trtsus (tṛtsu)
nodes.description: The Tṛtsus, Sudās's people in the battle of ten kings, confined to RV 7.18 and 7.83.

nodes.label: abscess (vidradha)
nodes.description: The vidradhá, an internal swelling or abscess, named with the red balāsa and the visalpaka as things a forest tree and a herb are told not to leave a bit of.

nodes.label: rice (vrīhi)
nodes.description: Rice, as the standing grain and as the husked grain of the cooked offering; almost entirely an Atharvavedic and Yajurvedic word.

nodes.label: limb-splitting (aṅgabheda)
nodes.description: The limb-splitter, paired in both its occurrences with the limb-waster and with heart-ache, in the two charms that expel head-disease by incantation.

nodes.label: earache (karṇaśūla)
nodes.description: Ear-pain, named twice in the head-disease charm of AVS 9.8 and nowhere else in the four Saṃhitās.

nodes.label: beans (māṣa)
nodes.description: The bean, named in the short lists of cultivated foods rather than described.

nodes.label: pallor (palita)
nodes.description: What is pale, named twice in the kilasa hymn beside the leprous spot and removed by the same herb. Kept apart from palitá "hoary" said of a man, which is the same string and a different thing.

nodes.label: wind-caused ailment (vātīkṛta)
nodes.description: The vātī́kṛta, "made by wind": an ailment named only in the two compounds the corpus prints for its remedies -- the viṣāṇakā herb that effaces it and the pippalī that is a remedy for it.

nodes.label: jātavedas (knower of all that is born)
wild animal (mṛga)
nodes.description: The wild animal as against the herd animal: the deer or beast of the waste, hunted, snared, and used as the image of anything that roams.

nodes.label: buffalo (mahiṣa)
nodes.description: The buffalo, dressed three hundred at a time in RV 5.29.7, and the same word applied to any bellowing power.

nodes.label: scorpion (vṛścika)
nodes.description: The scorpion or stinger, slain with a club at AVS 10.4.9, ground up with the constrictor at 10.4.15, and told at RV 1.191.16 that its venom is weak.

nodes.label: might (ojas)
nodes.description: Physical force and overpowering vigour, the quality by which a god prevails.

nodes.label: friendship (sakhya)
nodes.description: The bond of comradeship, invoked between the worshipper and the god as a claim rather than a sentiment.

nodes.label: help (avas)
nodes.description: The aid a god is asked to bring, the single most frequent request in the corpus.

nodes.label: offering call (svāhā)
nodes.description: The cry uttered at the moment the oblation is released, svaha, and its counterpart the vasat-call. 326 passages carry it: 155 in the Yajurveda and 157 in the Atharvaveda against 14 in the Rigveda and none at all in the Samaveda, which makes it the sharpest single lexical signature of a formulary in the corpus. VS 25.1 fires it twice in one breath, "śuklāya svāhā kṛṣṇāya svāhā".

nodes.label: light (jyotis)
nodes.description: Light as such: the brightness a god makes, finds or gives, distinct from the body that emits it.

nodes.label: body (tanū)
nodes.description: The body or bodily person, what is protected, healed, or offered along with the offering.

nodes.label: homage (namas)
nodes.description: Reverence offered in words and posture, the verbal accompaniment of an offering.

nodes.label: immortality (amṛta)
nodes.description: Deathlessness, the condition of the gods and the thing the sacrificer hopes the rite will extend to him.

nodes.label: truth (satya)
nodes.description: What is real and holds good, said of gods, of speech and of a promise.

nodes.label: fame (śravas)
nodes.description: Renown that outlasts a life, what a patron buys with liberality and a poet confers.

nodes.label: day (ahan)
nodes.description: The day as a unit of time, and the days as the succession a life is counted in.

nodes.label: darkness (tamas)
nodes.description: Darkness, both the night's and the hostile obscurity that light is asked to break.

nodes.label: battle (yudh)
nodes.description: Armed conflict, from the raid for cattle to the set battle in which a god is asked to take a side.

nodes.label: breath (prāṇa)
nodes.description: Breath as the vital current, in the Atharvaveda already treated as the thing whose departure is death.

nodes.label: desire (kāma)
nodes.description: Wanting: the wish a rite is performed to fulfil, and in a few late hymns a cosmic first principle.

nodes.label: heart (hṛd)
nodes.description: The heart as the inward place where a hymn is formed and an intention is held.

nodes.label: thriving (puṣṭi)
nodes.description: Thriving and increase asked for a household and its livestock, the fattening growth of what one already has rather than the acquisition of new goods.

nodes.label: gold (hiraṇya)
nodes.description: Gold, both as an object of wealth and as the colour of anything radiant.

nodes.label: ascetic heat (tapas)
nodes.description: Heat generated by austerity, treated as a productive power rather than as self-denial.

nodes.label: splendour (varcas)
nodes.description: Varcas, the lustre a person is quickened with or bound into an amulet for; the Atharvaveda's commonest single request word after wellbeing. Only the instrumental and dative are aliases: the bare stem sits inside brāhmaṇavarcasá and hastivarcasá, which are other people's splendour, and inside hatavarcasáḥ, which is its loss.

nodes.label: witchcraft (kṛtyā)
nodes.description: Witchcraft as a thing done to a person: the hostile spell, its maker, and the counter-charm that turns it back on him.

nodes.label: poison (viṣa)
nodes.description: Poison as a substance in the body, whether from a snake, an insect, a plant or a poisoned arrow, and the thing charms declare to be sapless.

nodes.label: pouring into the fire (homa)
nodes.description: The pouring of the oblation into the fire, spoken as it is done: "juhomi", I pour (28 passages), and "juhota", pour ye (11). VS 7.26 puts the act, the caller's cry and the strainer in one line: "whatever drop of thine leaps forth, from the adhvaryu's hand or from the filter, that I pour with my mind, made with the vasat-call, svaha".

nodes.label: fever (takman)
nodes.description: Takman, the Atharvaveda's fever: addressed in the second person, classified by its period (tertian, quartan, constant), by its season (autumnal, cold, hot, of the rainy season) and by its colour, and sent away to named foreign peoples. It has its own hymns -- AVS 1.25, 5.22, 6.20 -- and occurs nowhere outside the Atharvaveda.

nodes.label: affliction (amīvā)
nodes.description: Amīvā: sickness in general, the affliction a god is asked to smite or expel rather than a named complaint. The one member of this group that is a four-Veda word -- Soma, Brahmaṇaspati and Vāstoṣpati are each called amīvahán, "slayer of amīvā".

nodes.label: the malevolent (durhārd)
nodes.description: The evil-hearted: the hostile person as the Atharvaveda's charms treat him -- an affliction to be warded off, burnt against by darbha grass, gored by Agni's horns, and kept from a bride. All 26 token occurrences are Atharvavedic.

nodes.label: worms (krimi)
nodes.description: Worms and internal vermin, addressed as living enemies to be crushed and named by colour and habitat in the Atharvaveda's worm hymns.

nodes.label: ritual taking up (grahaṇa)
nodes.description: The act of taking an implement or an offering in hand, spoken in the first person while it is done: "gṛhṇāmi", I take. Twenty passages, twelve Yajurvedic, eight Atharvavedic and not one Rigvedic, which is what a formulary looks like measured against a hymn collection. The full formula is at VS 1.10 -- "by the impulse of god Savitar, with the arms of the Asvins, with the hands of Pusan, acceptable to Agni, I take thee".

nodes.label: imprecation (abhiśasti)
nodes.description: Imprecation and calumny, and the epithet abhiśastipā́ "protector against imprecation" that names it. Unlike the rest of this group it is not Atharvavedic property: 10 of its 18 token occurrences are Rigvedic or Yajurvedic.

nodes.label: ointment (āñjana)
nodes.description: The āñjana, the salve of the three-peaked mountain: addressed in the second person in AVS 4.9 and 19.44-45 as a protection that grinds up demons and sorceresses, told that fever, balāsa and the snake are its three slaves, and rubbed on by wives at a funeral. Its two names, traikakudá "of the three-peaked mountain" and "of the Yamunā", are folded in here because AVS 4.9.10 says they are both its names.

nodes.label: vedic student (brahmacārin)
nodes.description: The student under the discipline of study and chastity, the subject of AVS 11.5 and of RV 10.109.5.

nodes.label: bodily hurt (rapas)
nodes.description: Rapas: bodily hurt, blemish and defect -- the thing the wind is asked to blow away at AVS 4.13 and the thing Rudra is asked to carry one over at RV 2.33. Distinct from the root rap- "to prate", which is the same string in four other forms.

nodes.label: freedom from debt (ṛṇa)
nodes.description: Debt and the wish to be quit of it, owed to men, to the gods and to Death, and asked to be discharged rather than forgiven.

nodes.label: ill-named beings (durṇāman)
nodes.description: The durnaman, "the ill-named": a class of noxious beings blamed for attacks on pregnant women and infants, distinct from the rakshas of the demon hymns.

nodes.label: malignant sprite (arāya)
nodes.description: The arāyá: a noxious sprite blamed for wasting a person and for attacks on a woman, smitten away by a herb or an amulet. Whitney renders it variously "niggard", "sorceress" and "wizard (? arā́ya-)", which is recorded here because the inconsistency is his and not this file's.

nodes.label: assembly (sabhā)
nodes.description: The assembly and the gathering, "the two daughters of Prajāpati", as an occasion a man needs help at: to be favoured in, to be fit for, to speak what is pleasant in, and to have the witchcraft made against him there undone. sabhā́ and sámiti are folded together because AVS 7.12.1 and 15.9.2 name them as a pair.

nodes.label: existence (sat)
nodes.description: The existent, what is, as against what is not. In this corpus still a substantivised neuter participle of as- 'to be' and not yet a settled noun: it is predicated of things and asked after, as in the one Being the sages call by many names (RV 1.164.46), and it is not the Upanishadic Being. Distinct from satya 'truth', which is a different stem with its own entity, VG:CONCEPT:SATYA-TRUTH; the two alias sets are disjoint and neither leaks into the other.

nodes.label: curse (śapatha)
nodes.description: The spoken curse -- a rival's, a sister's, a priest's in fury -- sent back to the curser rather than cured, and the thing an amulet or a herb is said to keep off.

nodes.label: metal (ayas)
nodes.description: Metal, and specifically the dark metal the translators render "iron": the substance of Indra's bolt, of a fort, of a hook and of a blade.

nodes.label: non-existence (asat)
nodes.description: Non-existence: the asat of "there was neither non-existence nor existence then" (RV 10.129.1). Unlike sat it is already a noun in its own right -- the Rigvedic annotation lemmatises it asant-, separately from the root -- and existence is twice said to have sprung from it (RV 10.72.2-3). In the Atharvaveda it is one pole of a paired cosmological formula (AVS 4.1.1, 10.7.10, 17.1.19). Not filed under VG:CONCEPT:SAT-EXISTENCE: non-existence is not a kind of existence.

nodes.label: lead (sīsa)
nodes.description: Lead, used in the Atharvaveda as the material with which a demon is pierced and in the Yajurveda as one of the metals of the sacrifice.

nodes.label: debility (sedi)
nodes.description: Sedí, debility or failure: housed in an enemy's dwelling with the hags, wished onto an opposing army beside hunger and fear, and trodden down underfoot by the ploughman. Every token occurrence is Atharvavedic.

nodes.label: concluding bath (avabhṛtha)
nodes.description: The bath that ends a soma rite, addressed in the vocative as a power in its own right: "avabhṛtha nicumpuṇa ... with the Gods may I wash out the sin that I have sinned against the Gods, with men the sin against mankind" (VS 3.48, VS 8.27, VS 20.18). Its place in the rite is stated rather than inferred: VS 19.28 closes its chain of means with "sāmnāvabhṛtha āpyate", by the Saman the concluding bath is reached.

nodes.label: sorcerous attack (abhicāra)
nodes.description: Sorcery directed at a person, named in the two Atharvavedic verses where the apāmārga plant spoils it and the varaṇá tree shields against it.

nodes.label: bruise (kṣipta)
nodes.description: What is struck or bruised, named at AVS 6.109 only inside the compound that says the pippalī berry is its remedy, and once in the genitive beside the wind-ailment.

nodes.label: silver (rajata)
nodes.description: Silver, named beside gold and iron in the short metal lists and in the amulet charms.

nodes.label: copper (loha)
nodes.description: Copper or bronze, attested once: VS 18.13 asks that "my copper and my lead and my tin" prosper by sacrifice, in the corpus's one enumeration of the metals.

nodes.label: madness (unmāda)
nodes.description: Being crazed, in the one Atharvavedic verse that names it: crazed from sin against the gods or crazed from a demon, with the speaker declaring he knows the remedy.

nodes.label: dark metal (śyāma)
nodes.description: The dark metal named at VSM 18.13, standing inside that verse's metal enumeration between ayas and loha. The registry records the attested token and its position in that list; it does not assert a modern metallurgical identification, for which the traditional readings (iron, or a dark copper alloy) disagree. Only the exact inflected forms are registered: the bare stem token-matches the unrelated verb form śyāma at RV 6.5.7 and substring-matches 22 times inside aśyāma. `śyāmaṃ` is the Yajurvedic witness at VSM 18.13 and `śyāmam` the Atharvavedic one at AVS 11.3.7, one verse before the trapu witness in the same hymn.

nodes.label: tin (trapu)
nodes.description: Tin, named in the Atharvaveda's material description at AVS 11.3.8. The exact Sanskrit token is registered because the stored text already attests it; this entry does not infer metal absence from Vedas where that token is not matched.
